html:
SMTO-GWT-0016 — The Gateway couldn't read or save its security records

GUID: 5265f250-285c-409e-90ce-33d8cb4bf290
Slug: gateway-pairing-state-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The Gateway keeps files that remember which SMTO it trusts and which requests it has already seen. It couldn't read or save one of them, so it refused the request and ran nothing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway computer, make sure the disk has free space. A full disk stops the Gateway from saving the small records it needs for every request.
  2. Make sure the Gateway is started by the same user account and with the same settings as before. A different account or settings folder may not be able to open the Gateway's saved records.
  3. Restart the Gateway, then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection. A fresh start lets the Gateway open its records again once the cause is fixed.
  4. Only if the manager confirms the Gateway's saved link record is damaged and can't be restored from a backup, they can run its pairing reset command on that computer, then check the connection again. A reset replaces only the link to SMTO, so it is a last resort for a record that can't be repaired.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's row shows Connected and tasks run on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't delete the Gateway's settings folder; it holds the Gateway's identity and job history. A lost connection doesn't prove that earlier work didn't run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway could not validate or access its saved pairing record, or could not durably save replay-protection data; this does not by itself prove the pairing file is corrupt.

What this means

  • The Gateway could not validate or access its persisted pairing record, or could not safely persist replay-protection evidence. The shared category does not prove that the pairing file itself is corrupt. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway could not validate or access its persisted pairing record, or could not safely persist replay-protection evidence. The shared category does not prove that the pairing file itself is corrupt.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether the failure came from pairing-state load or nonce persistence; inspect permissions and storage errors while preserving existing trust records.

How to fix it

  • Inspect GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR/client-auth on the Gateway host: pairing.json must exist (an initialized marker without it is rejected), have a valid version/state/revision and a controller key matching its controller_id, and the directory must be writable for nonce records. Fix disk space, ownership and the OS account or state-directory setting used at startup; restore from backup if damaged, and use the local reset command (try --dry-run first) only if a deliberate pairing replacement is intended.
  • Repair access to the indicated Gateway state storage and preserve trusted identity records. Use the supported local reset only if an intentional pairing replacement is required.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Pairing state validates and authenticated requests can persist replay evidence under the intended controller.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
